ai.title: Fix lastMessage text extraction and tooluse ordering
ai.summary: Agent runtime now concatenates all assistant text chunks in `lastMessage` outputs instead of returning only the final segment, resolving truncated responses from streaming subagents. `stream-parser.ts` suppresses intermediate assistant text messages when tool calls are active to prevent Anthropic API validation errors caused by interleaved `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks. Changes affect `.agents/editor/best-of-n`, `.agents/file-explorer`, and `packages/agent-runtime`. `extractSpawnResults` logic was refactored to correctly unwrap nested `AgentOutput` values from JSON tool results.

eli5.text: When you ask the agent to do a task that involves breaking it into smaller subtasks (like having multiple assistants each write a draft and then picking the best one), the final summary you see now includes the complete text from each subtask instead of just the last fragment of it. The agent builds up its response in small pieces as it works, and a bug was causing only the very last piece to show up, cutting off the beginning. There was also a related problem where, if the agent decided to use a tool mid-response, the pieces were being arranged in an order that the underlying AI system rejected, which could cause the response to fail partway through. Both issues are now fixed, so subtasks that produce text reports and subtasks that call tools now complete and display their full results

ai.title: CLI test isolation
ai.summary: Added mock logger to `fetchUsageData` test in `cli/src/hooks/__tests__/use-usage-query.test.ts`. Isolates test from side effects by injecting mock `error`, `warn`, `info`, and `debug` functions. Prevents real logging during failed request assertions.

eli5.text: The engineers tweaked one of their automated tests so it no longer writes extra log messages when it checks that the program correctly reports a failed connection. This only matters to people making changes to the command-line tool itself - specifically to anyone reading or running that test suite. If you ran the test before the change, you might have seen stray 'error' or 'info' text appear in the terminal even when the test passed; after the change, that test stays quiet unless the failure message it expects actually appears.

ai.title: Context pruner now accounts for system prompt and tool definition
ai.summary: Context pruner calculates effective message budget by subtracting system prompt and tool definition tokens from maxContextLength. Previously, the pruner used the full maxContextLength for message history, ignoring the overhead of system prompts and tool schemas which could cause context overflow. The change introduces new optional fields systemPrompt and toolDefinitions in AgentState types across .agents/types/agent-definition.ts and common/src/types/session-state.ts. Tool definitions are serialized in packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts using mapValues to extract description and inputSchema for token counting.

eli5.text: When an AI helper runs out of thinking space, it used to forget your messages too soon because it didn't account for the space taken up by its own instructions and tool descriptions. Now it factors those in, so it keeps your conversation history longer before trimming. This matters to anyone using an AI agent that relies on multiple tools. You'd notice the helper stays on task longer without abruptly losing context. The fix is already live.

ai.title: Bundle local agents into CLI binary at build time
ai.summary: Added `scripts/prebuild-agents.ts` to scan `.agents/` and generate `src/agents/bundled-agents.generated.ts`. This embeds agent definitions into the CLI binary, removing runtime filesystem dependency for bundled agents. Updated `package.json` dev script and `scripts/build-binary.ts` to trigger generation. Refactored agent loading logic in `src/utils/local-agent-registry.ts` to consume bundled data, deleting `src/utils/load-agent-definitions.ts` and updating imports in `src/index.tsx`, `src/commands/publish.ts`, and hooks.

eli5.text: When you run the CLI tool, it now carries the agent definitions it needs inside the application itself, rather than going looking for them in hidden project folders every time. This means you no longer need certain extra files sitting around on disk for the built tool to work. The developers added a step that scans the agents folder and bakes their contents directly into the program files before it is packaged. You would notice this if you tried to run the tool without its usual agent files present, because it would still work the same as before.

ai.title: Revert lastMessage extraction and tool ordering fix
ai.summary: Reverts logic extracting all streaming text chunks and enforcing tool_use/tool_result ordering constraints. `stream-parser.ts` now pushes text chunks to `assistantMessages` regardless of pending `toolCalls`, while `editor-best-of-n.ts` and `file-picker.ts` revert to reading only the last assistant message or first structured output. Covers Agent Runtime stream handling and internal agent orchestration. Removes the guard preventing text accumulation when tool calls are present.

eli5.text: When an AI agent was running and using multiple tools at once (like asking several helpers to work on different parts of a task), it stopped reliably collecting all the written responses those helpers produced. The system had been gathering every text chunk that came in during the back-and-forth tool calls, but this change rolled that back, so now it only picks up the final message or the first structured output from each helper, potentially missing earlier parts of their responses. This affects internal AI agent workflows like editing multiple code versions or picking files, where complete helper feedback matters. It is live today.

ai.summary: Reverts prior patch in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tool-stream-parser.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/stream-parser.ts`. ai.title: Fix duplicate subagent output
ai.summary: Removed generic 'text' event handler from cli/src/utils/sdk-event-handlers.ts. Subagent text chunks now bypass sendSubagentChunk in packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agents.ts, writing directly to client via writeToClient. Prevents double rendering of subagent output in CLI.

eli5.text: If you run a subagent from the command line, its output no longer prints twice. It used to be handled by a generic text path and then again by the subagent path, so you'd see each reply duplicated. Now subagent output is sent straight to your terminal once, while regular text still flows through the normal path.

ai.title: CLI /publish command adds interactive agent selection UI
ai.summary: Adds /publish slash command with interactive agent selection UI via new React components and state store. Replaces console-based flow with structured PublishResult return type and command registry integration. Covers CLI chat input, command handlers, and publish mutation hooks; shared API types updated in common/src/types/api/agents/publish.ts. Agent checklist supports recursive dependency tree rendering and pre-selection via command arguments.

eli5.text: When you type /publish in the command-line chat, you now get a selectable checklist of your local agents to pick from instead of the old text prompt. The checklist shows each agent plus how many other agents it depends on, and you can pre-select some by listing them right after the command. Once you confirm, the tool tries to upload the chosen agents and reports plain success-or-failure feedback. This is live today for anyone running the updated command-line tool.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.540 ships context pruning, publish UI, and bundled agents
ai.summary: CLI 1.0.540 consolidates a day of same-day work across cli, packages/agent-runtime, and .agents into release package.json. The context pruner now preserves tool-call/tool-result pairs and uses media-aware token counting (1000 tokens per image), while the CLI bundles local agent definitions into the binary at build time via scripts/prebuild-agents.ts, removing the runtime filesystem dependency for bundled agents. The new /publish slash command adds an interactive agent selection UI with recursive dependency-tree rendering and pre-selection via arguments, replacing the prior console-based flow with a structured PublishResult return type.
ai.evidence: The diff to `cli/release/package.json` shows `"version": "1.0.539"` changed to `"version": "1.0.540"`. Analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump commit that consolidates the same-day user-visible release updates listed under the 1.0.540 release instructions.

eli5.text: Version 1.0.540 of the Freebuff CLI introduces three major improvements: built-in AI agents are now packaged directly inside the application, a new /publish command lets you interactively share your own agents, and the conversation history automatically trims itself to avoid hitting limits. The context trimming is smarter now. It keeps track of paired actions and responses so they are never cut apart, and it reserves space for instructions and tool definitions, which prevents errors when conversations get long. Mouse support has also been added to suggestion menus, so you can click on autocomplete options instead of only navigating with the keyboard. On top of that, duplicate text in sub-agent outputs has been fixed, making streamed responses cleaner and easier to read. Upgrading gives you a more reliable and user-friendly experience with fewer glitches during long coding sessions. The bundled agents mean things work offline without depending on external files, and the new publishing UI makes sharing your custom agents much simpler.

ai.title: Fix SDK type exports and add type testing script
ai.summary: Updated sdk/src/index.ts to export buildUserMessageContent from local relative path instead of @codebuff/agent-runtime/util/messages, fixing type resolution. Added sdk/scripts/test-types.ts to run type checks across cjs-compatibility, esm-compatibility, and ripgrep-bundling subprojects. Added test:types npm script to sdk/package.json. Script removes stale node_modules/@codebuff/sdk before setup and ensures dist build exists.

eli5.text: If you build tools or apps that rely on this toolkit, you may have hit confusing type errors, especially around message-building helpers, even though everything looked correct on the surface. The toolkit now imports those helpers from its own internal location instead of an external package path that was causing mismatches, so type checking resolves properly. A new command was also added to the toolkit’s build steps that automatically tests type compatibility across different project setups, removing leftover cached copies first to ensure a clean check. The fix applies today to anyone installing or updating the toolkit, and you’d notice fewer mysterious type failures when integrating it into projects that use strict module or bundling settings.

ai.title: Consolidate SDK verification scripts
ai.summary: Added `sdk/scripts/verify.ts` to orchestrate build, typecheck, smoke tests, and compatibility checks, replacing scattered `package.json` scripts like `build:verify` and `test:types`. This unifies non-traditional test execution into a single `bun run verify` command, with `--skip-build` support for faster iteration. Scope limited to SDK tooling; no runtime code changes.

eli5.text: You, as a developer working on this software kit, no longer need to remember several different commands to check that everything works, there's now a single command that builds the software, checks for code errors, and runs all the compatibility tests at once. The team replaced the old collection of separate instructions in the project file with one new verification script, and added a shortcut to skip the build step if you just want to run the tests quickly. You'd see this as one command replacing several, and if you looked, you'd find the old separate scripts are gone and a single new one in their place.

ai.title: Filter CLI @ menu to current agent subagents
ai.summary: The '@' menu in CLI now filters bundled agents to show only subagents of the current base agent mode. `loadLocalAgents` accepts an optional `AgentMode` to determine the `spawnableAgents` list from the active agent definition. User-defined agents in `.agents/` remain visible regardless of mode. The agent cache is updated to key by `agentMode` instead of storing a single global list.

eli5.text: When you open the '@' assistant picker in the app, it now shows only the helper assistants that go with whichever main assistant you're currently using, plus your own custom ones from your local folder. Previously it tried to list every bundled helper at once, which mixed assistants that don't belong together. So if you switch between different base assistants, the menu updates to match the right crew, while your personal '.agents/' folder entries stay available no matter what.

ai.title: SDK e2e tests update model to claude-sonnet-4.5
ai.summary: SDK e2e tests replace anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514 with anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 in AgentDefinition model fields. Updates cover custom-agents/api-integration-agent, database-query-agent, and weather-agent test files. Change ensures test suites validate against the newer Sonnet model.

eli5.text: The sample helper bots used in the SDK's end-to-end tests, the ones the engineering team runs to make sure everything works, are now being compared against the newest version of Anthropic's Claude model instead of the older one. If you ran the test suite locally or in CI right now, those three agents would talk to 'claude-sonnet-4.5' rather than 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514', so the checks now validate that integration with the fresher model version passes. Nothing changed for real users' bots yet; this only bumps the model name inside throwaway test fixtures that live in the repo.

ai.title: SDK custom tools JSON Schema serialization
ai.summary: SDK custom tools now serialize Zod input schemas to JSON Schema via `z.toJSONSchema` in `sdk/src/run-state.ts` to survive JSON transport. `packages/agent-runtime` uses `ensureZodSchema` and `zod-from-json-schema` to convert JSON schemas back to Zod before validation in `tool-executor.ts` and `prompts.ts`. `common/src/util/file.ts` updates `customToolDefinitionsSchema` to accept both Zod and JSON Schema objects.

eli5.text: When you define a custom tool for an assistant built with the SDK, its input rules were getting lost while being sent between systems, so the assistant could no longer understand or validate what arguments the tool expected. Now those input rules are translated into a universal format that survives being transmitted as data, and then converted back into a working validator on the other side, so custom tools reliably accept and check their inputs again. If you looked at this release you would see your custom tool definitions now serialize cleanly with no errors when passed through JSON-based transport.

ai.title: SDK v0.10.0
ai.summary: Bump @codebuff/sdk to 0.10.0. Introduces native tool calls under the hood. Public API changes minimal. Covers sdk/CHANGELOG.md, sdk/package.json.

eli5.text: If you use the toolkit that developers rely on to build with Codebuff, you're now on version 0.10.0. Behind the scenes, the toolkit can now make native tool calls, which means it interacts with the model more directly and efficiently, though the parts you see and use haven't changed much. This update is live today and is meant to make future features easier to add, without requiring any action from you.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.541 bundles subagent filtering, SDK tool serialization
ai.summary: CLI 1.0.541 ships as a release-bump consolidating the same-day work across cli, sdk, and packages/agent-runtime. The @ menu now filters bundled agents to subagents of the current base agent mode via an optional AgentMode parameter in loadLocalAgents, while user-defined .agents/ entries stay visible. The SDK advances to v0.10.0 with native tool calls under the hood, custom tool Zod schemas now serialize to JSON Schema in sdk/src/run-state.ts and round-trip back to Zod via ensureZodSchema in tool-executor.ts and prompts.ts. SDK verification is also consolidated into a single bun run verify script and flaky e2e tests were skipped to keep CI stable.
ai.evidence: Commit a946443f modifies only cli/release/package.json, bumping the version string from 1.0.540 to 1.0.541. The same-day release context lists 7 prior commits spanning CLI, SDK, and agent-runtime packages as the user-visible content of this release.

eli5.text: Version 1.0.541 adds subagent filtering to the command-line interface, updates SDK end-to-end tests to use a newer AI model, and improves how custom tools are serialized for the SDK. The main highlights are threefold. First, the '@' menu in the CLI now shows only the subagents relevant to the agent mode you are currently using, so you see fewer irrelevant options when picking an assistant to work with. Second, the SDK now properly converts custom tool schemas into JSON Schema format before sending them over, and converts them back into the format the agent needs before validation, which prevents tool definitions from breaking during data transfer. Third, the bundled SDK version bumps to 0.10.0, which now handles native tool calls under the hood, and a single 'verify' command replaces the old scattered verification scripts, making it faster to run all build, typecheck, and compatibility checks at once. Additionally, four flaky or broken end-to-end tests around knowledge and project files are now marked as skipped, preventing them from failing builds while a proper fix is developed. Upgrading to this version gives you a cleaner agent selection experience, more reliable custom tool handling when building with the SDK, and a faster one-command way to verify your SDK builds and tests. You also stay on the latest SDK with native tool-call support, and you avoid CI failures caused by the known-broken end-to-end tests.

ai.title: Remove local agents toggle from CLI
ai.summary: Deleted local agents display logic and toggle from cli/src/app.tsx. User should use '@' command instead. Refactor removes agentCount, formatIdentifier, renderAgentListItem, and associated ToolCallItem rendering.

eli5.text: If you open the command-line assistant today, the pop-up list of your locally saved agents no longer appears in the main header. Instead, typing '@' will now bring up agent selection, replacing the old toggle that showed agent counts and names directly. Behind the scenes, the code that built and displayed that local agent list has been removed, trimming away roughly 50 lines while adding just one. This is live now, so the next time you launch the tool you will only see the '@' shortcut instead of the former agent panel.

ai.title: Remove eager CLI agent validation
ai.summary: Agent validation now runs lazily inside useAgentValidation instead of during CLI startup in index.tsx. App and Chat components no longer receive loadedAgentsData or validationErrors props. The hook filters network errors via filterNetworkErrors before setting state. This removes redundant validation calls and simplifies component prop drilling.

eli5.text: If you start the command-line assistant, it no longer immediately checks every available agent right away. Instead, it waits until you actually need that check, like when you send your first message, then quietly filters out only the network-related validation problems before showing you anything. You won't see a burst of early validation errors on startup anymore, and the program won't waste time double-checking the same agents twice during launch.
